FM15.reasoning: The agent only optimizes and evaluates using RMSE on the original, exponentially-transformed Price scale, which is highly sensitive to outliers, without verifying if a more robust metric like MAE or RMSLE would be better suited for the heavily skewed target.

other_failure_modes.name: Test-set group statistics calculation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes group-level statistics (like mean or min/max by category) independently on the test set using only test set data. This causes a severe train-test distribution mismatch because small groups in the test set will have wildly different statistic values compared to the robust averages computed on the training set.

other_failure_modes.name: Cross-fold data leakage during imputation and TF-IDF
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes statistics like the median for imputation and fits TF-IDF vectorizers on the entire training set before splitting it into cross-validation folds. This leaks validation fold information into the training folds, making the out-of-fold validation scores overly optimistic.

summary: The agent implements a strong end-to-end pipeline with out-of-fold target encoding, a PyTorch TabularGatedNet, and SLSQP ensemble blending. However, it introduces a critical feature engineering bug by computing group statistics independently on the test set, leading to a train-test distribution mismatch. Additionally, it suffers from cross-fold leakage during imputation and TF-IDF fitting, and optimizes its ensemble solely for RMSE on a highly skewed target.
